newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha edges up on crude bounce, N+A demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha edges up on crude bounce, N+A demand.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices rose slightly on Tuesday after a bounce in crude oil futures and continued signs of tighter supply of heavy naphthenic and aromatic (N+A) material, traders and brokers said.

June swaps, which have resisted the recent selloff in crude oil, rose about $1.50 to $181/$182 a tonne, with July at the same level. NWE cargoes were notionally valued $1 higher at $183/$185 cif, with no deals heard done yet.
"It has not gone down as much as the crude oil because the market is considered quite tight...It is slightly shorter than it is long," one broker said, citing seasonal factors.
Reformer demand for the heavier material to make gasoline was being given an extra boost by recent cuts in refinery runs, he said. In many cases the reformers were still producing gasoline, he said.
At the same time, petrochemical demand for lighter material of 80-plus paraffins, due to its competitiveness to LPG, was supporting those prices, he said.

A trader at a Belgian refinery, however, warned that the narrowing differential between heavier naphtha and fob Rotterdam gasoline prices may soon make naphtha relatively expensive. That spread is now near $13 a tonne and, at least for his refinery, a spread of $20 is usually optimal.
"In general, heavy naphtha is quite tight," he said. "If you're looking for good quality naphtha you can't find it."
He sold the equivalent of 15,000 tonnes of heavier material in the last few weeks on a quotes-related basis to a major European refiner.
